input.question: Does putting two engines on the same aircraft give it double the thrust?
input.ground_truth: Yes, thrust will double so long as the engines are far enough apart to avoid interacting with each other. Acceleration, top speed and other proformance indicators will not double and may even decreace due to the added weight and drag of a second engine however.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Does putting two engines on the same aircraft give it double the thrust?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Let’s imagine a toy car. If you put two motors on it, it might go faster, right? But with airplanes, it’s a little more tricky.

If you put two engines on an airplane, it usually gives the plane more power to go faster or carry more stuff. But it doesn’t always mean the plane gets “double” the push (that’s what thrust means). Sometimes the plane can only use so much push at once, or the two engines might get in each other’s way a little bit.

So, two engines can give more power, but not always exactly double the thrust. It depends on how the engines and the airplane are built!
